notes.front: What is emergency response information (ERI)?
notes.back: Information that can be used to mitigate an incident involving hazardous materials, containing at least seven listed items.
notes.explanation: Section 172.602(a) defines the term for the subpart and sets the minimum content every ERI must hold.
notes.example: Like the safety card in an aircraft seat pocket, but written for whoever deals with a spill, fire or leak of the hazardous material in a shipment.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: the term ‘‘emergency response information’’ means information that can be used in the mitigation of an incident involving hazardous materials and, as a minimum, must contain the following information:

notes.front: Which ERI element identifies the material itself?
notes.back: The basic description and technical name of the hazardous material.
notes.explanation: It is the same basic description and technical name that the shipping paper rules require.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (1) The basic description and technical name of the hazardous material as required by §§ 172.202 and 172.203(k), the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code, or the TDG Regulations, as appropriate (IBR, see § 171.7 of this subchapter); (2) Immediate hazards to health; (3) Risks of fire or explosion;

notes.front: Which ERI element deals with dangers to people’s health?
notes.back: Immediate hazards to health.
notes.explanation: Health is listed as its own item, second after the identity of the material.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (1) The basic description and technical name of the hazardous material as required by §§ 172.202 and 172.203(k), the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code, or the TDG Regulations, as appropriate (IBR, see § 171.7 of this subchapter); (2) Immediate hazards to health; (3) Risks of fire or explosion;

notes.front: Which ERI element states whether the material may burn or explode?
notes.back: Risks of fire or explosion.
notes.explanation: It sits beside the health hazards as a separate required element.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (1) The basic description and technical name of the hazardous material as required by §§ 172.202 and 172.203(k), the ICAO Technical Instructions, the IMDG Code, or the TDG Regulations, as appropriate (IBR, see § 171.7 of this subchapter); (2) Immediate hazards to health; (3) Risks of fire or explosion;

notes.front: Which ERI element says what to do at once after an accident or incident?
notes.back: Immediate precautions to be taken in the event of an accident or incident.
notes.explanation: It is one of the elements marked as immediate in § 172.602(a).
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (3) Risks of fire or explosion; (4) Immediate precautions to be taken in the event of an accident or incident; (5) Immediate methods for handling fires; (6) Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire; and (7) Preliminary first aid measures.

notes.front: Which ERI element covers how to deal with fires?
notes.back: Immediate methods for handling fires.
notes.explanation: Fires and spills are covered by two separate elements.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (3) Risks of fire or explosion; (4) Immediate precautions to be taken in the event of an accident or incident; (5) Immediate methods for handling fires; (6) Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire; and (7) Preliminary first aid measures.

notes.front: Which ERI element covers spills or leaks when there is no fire?
notes.back: Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire.
notes.explanation: This element is expressly for the case where no fire is involved.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (3) Risks of fire or explosion; (4) Immediate precautions to be taken in the event of an accident or incident; (5) Immediate methods for handling fires; (6) Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire; and (7) Preliminary first aid measures.

notes.front: Which ERI element covers treating people who are hurt?
notes.back: Preliminary first aid measures.
notes.explanation: It is the last of the seven minimum elements listed in § 172.602(a).
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (3) Risks of fire or explosion; (4) Immediate precautions to be taken in the event of an accident or incident; (5) Immediate methods for handling fires; (6) Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire; and (7) Preliminary first aid measures.

notes.front: An ERI sheet for a toxic liquid gives its basic description and technical name, health hazards, fire risks, immediate precautions, firefighting methods and first aid. Which required element is missing?
notes.back: B: Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire.
notes.choices:
A) The name of the carrier
B) Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire
C) The date the material was made
D) The packing instructions for the drum
notes.choicesExplained: A: The carrier’s name is not one of the seven elements. D: Packing instructions are not an ERI element. C: The date of manufacture is not an ERI element.
notes.explanation: The sheet holds six of the seven minimum elements of § 172.602(a).
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(a), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (3) Risks of fire or explosion; (4) Immediate precautions to be taken in the event of an accident or incident; (5) Immediate methods for handling fires; (6) Initial methods for handling spills or leaks in the absence of fire; and (7) Preliminary first aid measures.

notes.front: Where must ERI be available for use, relative to the package?
notes.back: Away from the package containing the hazardous material.
notes.explanation: Section 172.602(b)(2) sets this alongside the rules on language and on the documents that may carry it.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(b)(2), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (2) Available for use away from the package containing the hazardous material; and

notes.front: In what documents may ERI be presented?
notes.back: On the shipping paper, or in another document that also gives the basic description and technical name, such as a safety data sheet.
notes.explanation: A document such as a safety data sheet qualifies only if it also carries the basic description and technical name.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(b)(3), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (3) Presented— (i) On a shipping paper; (ii) In a document, other than a shipping paper, that includes both the basic description and technical name of the hazardous material as required by §§ 172.202 and 172.203(k),

notes.front: A shipper prints the first aid and firefighting advice only on a sticker on each drum, with nothing in the cab. Does this meet § 172.602(b)?
notes.back: A: No; ERI must be available for use away from the package.
notes.choices:
A) No; ERI must be available for use away from the package
B) Yes, if the sticker is in English
C) Yes, because labels already show the hazard
D) No; ERI may appear only on the shipping paper
notes.choicesExplained: B: English is required, but so is availability away from the package. C: Labels are not ERI. D: Another document, such as a safety data sheet, may also carry ERI.
notes.explanation: Information on the package alone does not meet the rule that it be usable away from the package.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(b)(2), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (2) Available for use away from the package containing the hazardous material; and

notes.front: Under § 172.602(b)(1) as amended from 3 September 2026, in what forms may ERI be printed legibly in English?
notes.back: Either in hard copy printed on paper or in electronic format.
notes.explanation: Hard copy on paper remains allowed; electronic format is an alternative to it.
notes.source: Hazardous Materials: Reducing Undue Paperwork Burdens to Domestic Carriers, 91 FR 49325 (final rule, 4 August 2026), § 172.602(b)(1) as amended, PDF p. 5
notes.evidence: (1) Printed legibly in English (either in hard copy printed on paper or in electronic format);

notes.front: In October 2026, a domestic highway carrier’s driver holds the ERI for the load on a tablet in the cab, legible and in English, and no paper copy. Does this meet § 172.602(b)(1)?
notes.back: C: Yes; electronic format is allowed since 3 September 2026.
notes.choices:
A) No; ERI must always be printed on paper
B) Only if the shipper emails a copy to the carrier each day
C) Yes; electronic format is allowed since 3 September 2026
D) No; ERI must be held by the shipper, not the carrier
notes.choicesExplained: A: That was the rule before the 2026 amendment. B: The amended rule sets no emailing condition. D: Carriers must keep ERI during transport under § 172.602(c)(1).
notes.explanation: The amended paragraph allows ERI in hard copy or in electronic format.
notes.source: Hazardous Materials: Reducing Undue Paperwork Burdens to Domestic Carriers, 91 FR 49325 (final rule, 4 August 2026), § 172.602(b)(1) as amended, PDF p. 5
notes.evidence: (1) Printed legibly in English (either in hard copy printed on paper or in electronic format);

notes.front: How must a carrier maintain ERI while transporting a hazardous material?
notes.back: In the same manner as shipping papers, immediately accessible to drivers and other crew in the event of an incident.
notes.explanation: Aircraft and vessels follow their own documents: the notification of pilot-in-command and the dangerous cargo manifest.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(c)(1), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: in the same manner as prescribed for shipping papers, except that the information must be maintained in the same manner aboard aircraft as the notification of pilot-in-command, and aboard vessels in the same manner as the dangerous cargo manifest. This information must be immediately accessible to train crew personnel, drivers of motor vehicles,

notes.front: A truck driver keeps the shipping paper in the door holder but the ERI in a toolbox on the trailer. What is the problem?
notes.back: D: ERI must be kept in the same manner as the shipping paper, immediately accessible to the driver.
notes.choices:
A) None; ERI may be kept anywhere on the vehicle
B) ERI must be carried by the shipper, not the carrier
C) ERI is needed only at facilities, not on the road
D) ERI must be kept in the same manner as the shipping paper, immediately accessible to the driver
notes.choicesExplained: A: The location is regulated, not left open. B: Each carrier must maintain the ERI. C: Carriers and facility operators both have duties.
notes.explanation: Section 172.602(c)(1) ties the ERI to the handling of shipping papers and to immediate access by drivers.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(c)(1), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: in the same manner as prescribed for shipping papers, except that the information must be maintained in the same manner aboard aircraft as the notification of pilot-in-command, and aboard vessels in the same manner as the dangerous cargo manifest. This information must be immediately accessible to train crew personnel, drivers of motor vehicles,

notes.front: When must the operator of a facility that receives, stores or handles hazmat in transportation keep ERI, and where?
notes.back: Whenever the hazardous material is present, in a location immediately accessible to facility personnel.
notes.explanation: The duty lasts for as long as the hazardous material is at the facility.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.602(c)(2), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: (2) Facility operators. Each operator of a facility where a hazardous material is received, stored or handled during transportation, shall maintain the information required by paragraph (a) of this section whenever the hazardous material is present. This information must be in a location that is immediately accessible to facility personnel

notes.front: Which hazardous materials fall outside the ERI subpart altogether?
notes.back: Those excepted from the shipping paper requirements.
notes.explanation: The ERI subpart follows the shipping paper rules: no shipping paper required, no ERI required.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.600(d), PDF p. 301
notes.evidence: (d) Exceptions. The requirements of this subpart do not apply to hazardous material which is excepted from the shipping paper requirements of this subchapter.

notes.front: What emergency response telephone number must a person offering a hazardous material provide?
notes.back: A numeric number, including the area code, for use in an emergency involving the hazardous material.
notes.explanation: Section 172.604(a) puts this duty on the person who offers the material for transportation.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: A person who offers a hazardous material for transportation must provide a numeric emergency response telephone number, including the area code, for use in an emergency involving the hazardous material. For telephone

notes.front: Where on the shipping paper must the emergency response telephone number be entered?
notes.back: Immediately after the description of the hazardous material, or once, prominently, if it applies to every hazardous material listed.
notes.explanation: A single entry must be prominent, readily identifiable and clearly visible.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a)(3), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: (3) Entered on a shipping paper, as follows: (i) Immediately following the description of the hazardous material required by subpart C of this part; or (ii) Entered once on the shipping paper in the manner prescribed in paragraph (b) of this section in a prominent, readily identifiable, and clearly visible manner

notes.front: When must the emergency response telephone number be monitored?
notes.back: At all times the hazardous material is in transportation, including storage incidental to transportation.
notes.explanation: Storage incidental to transportation counts, so the number cannot go quiet while the material waits at a terminal.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a)(1), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: (1) Monitored at all times the hazardous material is in transportation, including storage incidental to transportation;

notes.front: Does a number answered by an answering service that calls back meet the emergency telephone rule?
notes.back: No. A number that requires a call back, such as an answering service, answering machine or beeper, does not comply.
notes.explanation: The number must reach a knowledgeable person, or someone with immediate access to one.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a)(2), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: or has immediate access to a person who possesses such knowledge and information. A telephone number that requires a call back (such as an answering service, answering machine, or beeper device) does not meet the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section; and

notes.front: If an ERI provider’s number is used, who must be identified on the shipping paper next to the emergency response telephone number?
notes.back: The person registered with the ERI provider, by name, contract number or other unique identifier.
notes.explanation: The identifier goes immediately before, after, above or below the telephone number.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(b)(2), PDF p. 303
notes.evidence: The person who is registered with the ERI provider must be identified by name, or contract number or other unique identifier assigned by the ERI provider, on the shipping paper immediately before, after, above, or below the emergency response telephone number

notes.front: A small shipper gives its office number, staffed 8 am to 5 pm on weekdays, as the emergency response number for a load that travels overnight and waits at a terminal all weekend. Does this comply?
notes.back: C: No; the number must be monitored at all times the material is in transportation.
notes.choices:
A) Yes, because the material is not moving at the weekend
B) Yes, as long as the number is numeric and has an area code
C) No; the number must be monitored at all times the material is in transportation
D) Yes, if the driver also carries the ERI
notes.choicesExplained: B: Format is only one requirement; monitoring is another. A: Storage incidental to transportation still counts. D: Carrying ERI does not replace a monitored number.
notes.explanation: Storage incidental to transportation is included, so weekends at the terminal are covered too.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a)(1), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: (1) Monitored at all times the hazardous material is in transportation, including storage incidental to transportation;

notes.front: A shipper’s emergency number goes to voicemail, which promises a call back within 15 minutes from a chemist. Does it comply with § 172.604?
notes.back: A: No; a number that requires a call back does not comply.
notes.choices:
A) No; a number that requires a call back does not comply
B) Yes, if the call back comes within 15 minutes
C) Yes, because the chemist is knowledgeable
D) No; only government numbers may be used
notes.choicesExplained: C: The caller must reach knowledge directly, not wait for it. B: No call-back time makes a call-back number acceptable. D: The number may be the offeror’s or an organisation that accepts the responsibility.
notes.explanation: The rule names answering services, answering machines and beepers as examples of numbers that fail.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a)(2), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: A telephone number that requires a call back (such as an answering service, answering machine, or beeper device) does not meet the requirements of paragraph (a) of this section; and

notes.front: A shipping paper lists three hazardous materials, all covered by the same monitored emergency number. How may the number be entered?
notes.back: A: Once, prominently, marked as the emergency response number.
notes.choices:
A) Once, prominently, marked as the emergency response number
B) Only on the back of the last page
C) It may be left off because one number covers all three
D) Only in the certification
notes.choicesExplained: B: It must be easy to find, which a back page is not. C: The number is still required. D: The certification is not one of the places the rule allows.
notes.explanation: The single entry is allowed only when the number applies to every hazardous material on the paper and is labelled as the emergency number.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(a)(3), PDF p. 302
notes.evidence: The offeror may use one of the methods prescribed in this paragraph only if the telephone number applies to each hazardous material entered on the shipping paper, and if it is indicated that the telephone number is for emergency response information

notes.front: Which shipments are outside the emergency response telephone number requirement, among others?
notes.back: Materials offered under the limited quantity or excepted quantity provisions, and materials described under certain listed shipping names.
notes.explanation: The exception is from the requirements of § 172.604 itself, the telephone number section.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.604(d), PDF p. 303
notes.evidence: (d) The requirements of this section do not apply to— (1) Hazardous materials that are offered for transportation under the provisions applicable to limited quantities or excepted quantities; or (2) Materials properly described under the following shipping names:

notes.front: What must a carrier instruct its drivers to do after an incident involving a hazardous material for which a shipping paper is required?
notes.back: Contact the carrier, for example by telephone or mobile radio.
notes.explanation: The duty is on the carrier to give the instruction, for every mode of transport.
notes.source: 49 CFR Part 172 (Revised as of October 1, 2025), § 172.606(a), PDF p. 303
notes.evidence: (a) Each carrier who transports or accepts for transportation a hazardous material for which a shipping paper is required shall instruct the operator of a motor vehicle, train, aircraft, or vessel to contact the carrier (e.g., by telephone or mobile radio) in the event of an incident involving the hazardous material.
